title: Washing and pressing finished cross-stitch
subtitle: Removing handling marks and setting the stitches
excerpt: Finished cross-stitch is washed in cool water to remove handling oils and hoop marks, then pressed face-down on a terry towel to set the stitches without flattening them. The wash lifts any marks the hoop has left on the Aida; the pressing makes the fabric lie flat for framing.
sourceNotes: Washing and pressing methods for cross-stitch documented in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776, finishing chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: The process of pinning or pressing washed cross-stitch to shape while the fabric is still damp. For Aida, pressing face-down on a towel is the standard method. It sets the grid square, removes distortion caused by the hoop, and prepares the piece for framing.

content.text: Finished cross-stitch benefits from a gentle wash before framing. Handling deposits skin oil onto the fabric; the hoop leaves a ring; and some thread colours can bleed slightly. A cool-water wash addresses all three. The pressing step sets the Aida grid flat and removes any distortion the hoop introduced.
is not complicated for Aida-backed cross-stitch: press face-down on a folded terry towel. The stitches sit in the towel pile and are protected from the iron.
Touch a damp cotton bud to a strand of the darkest thread colour and blot on white paper. If colour transfers, wash each colour separately or skip the wash and go straight to pressing.
Soak in cool water for five minutes.
Fill a basin with cool water and a small amount of gentle textile wash. Lay the piece in the water without rubbing or wringing. Let it soak for five minutes.
Rinse and roll in a clean towel.
Lift the piece from the water without wringing. Lay it on a clean dry towel, roll the towel up with the piece inside, and press gently to absorb excess water. Do not twist.
Lay face-down on a folded terry towel.
Place the damp piece with the stitched side facing the towel. The towel pile cushions the stitches so they are not flattened by the iron.
Press with a medium-heat iron on the cotton setting.
Use a steam iron or a pressing cloth. Press gently without dragging the iron: drag can distort the Aida grid. Lift and place, working across the whole piece.
Leave the pressed piece flat on the towel until fully dry before framing. Framing a damp piece risks the fabric relaxing once it is behind glass.
